events.body:
Trip was RydeX, a non-metered fixed-quote service: F4 (billed 14.0 km, no excess) and F6 ($30.99 fixed, no toll/extra item) show the fare is a quote, so the off-route km in F3 cannot enter the fare even though the extra 4.08 km is real [F3][F4][F6][RD-1][RD-2].

RD-1 is satisfied: F3 is an off-route segment of 5.74 km where the optimal route covers 1.66 km (+4.08 km), and it must be screened against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not exempt it. There is no traffic-incident fact on the replaced stretch — F14 records none — and the only speed record is F11, a band-2 speed band on Central Expressway, which under RD-4(b) is corroboration at most and cannot exempt on its own; F12 and F13 concern other expressways [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4(a)][RD-4(b)].

RD-5 does exempt it. F7 (22:29, before the 22:33 segment start) has the driver proposing "go round via Lower Delta Road", and F8 (22:29 rider: "Sure, go ahead.") is the rider's own message agreeing to that named road; the chat is complete and fully timestamped (F9), and F10 is the driver's later statement, which alone would not be consent under G11 [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. This is a specific named road, but the agreement is to a driver-proposed route detour, not to the driver's own errand, so it is not an RD-5 case-(2) "errand elsewhere". The record does not positively place the segment on Lower Delta Road, so the segment is undetermined on the tie-to-the-road point (G13); it also cannot be swept under RD-3, since no stop was requested or measured (F3, F7, F8) [F3][F7][F8][RD-3(a)][RD-5].

Because the fare is a fixed quote, an undetermined finding changes neither the amount nor any account flag, so the case can still be ruled rather than sent to a person: there is nothing to refund and no basis for escalation [F4][F6][RD-2][RD-6].

Amount: no refund. F6 shows the fare was fully fixed ($3.90 base + $19.67 distance + $5.95 time + $1.47 platform = $30.99) with no distance surcharge or unpublished add-on to strip out, so recoverable amount = $0 [F4][F5][F6][RD-2].

Account flag: not applicable. F17 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's "repeated breach" condition is not met [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read F7, F8 and the complaint — a route discussion about a jam and a "go ahead" agreement; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 escalation [F7][F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 22:33:30 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes no amount (fixed fare) and no flag: if you cannot settle it, undetermined is allowed and the case may still be ruled. Evidence — F7: Chat #1 22:29 driver: “Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Lower Delta Road?”; F8: Chat #2 22:29 rider: “Sure, go ahead.”; F10: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Traffic was building up ahead so I asked the rider before turning off via Lower Delta Road and the rider agreed.” (F7, F8, F10)
